title: ELITE Study Electrical Impedance Tomography-guided Long-term Evaluation of Infants with Congenital Lung Malformations - Trajectories and Phenotypes
summary:
ELITE Study – Assessment of Lung Function in Newborn Infants with Congenital Lung Malformations

Newborn infants with congenital lung malformations, such as congenital diaphragmatic hernia or cystic lung abnormalities, often experience breathing difficulties and may require respiratory support or mechanical ventilation after birth.

The ELITE study aims to investigate lung development and function in these infants during the first hours of life and throughout their hospital stay. For this purpose, electrical impedance tomography (EIT) is used. EIT is a painless, radiation-free monitoring technique that uses an electrode belt placed around the chest to continuously visualize how air is distributed within the lungs.

The study consists of six substudies assessing lung function at different stages of clinical care: immediately after birth, during mechanical ventilation, during weaning from respiratory support, and during medically indicated bronchoscopies and respiratory physiotherapy. In addition, the study investigates whether EIT can provide information about blood flow within the lungs.

In one randomized substudy, infants are assigned by chance to one of two treatment groups to investigate whether adjusting ventilator pressure based on EIT measurements offers advantages compared with standard clinical care.

In selected infants, blood and respiratory samples are also analyzed to better understand the biological and molecular characteristics of their lung diseases.

The overall goal of the ELITE study is to improve our understanding of lung function and disease progression in these vulnerable newborn infants and to support the development of more individualized and lung-protective respiratory treatment strategies in the future.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All preterm and term neonates (>24 weeks of gestation) with congenital lung malformations (CLM) who are hospitalized in the Department of Neonatology or Pediatric Intensive Care Medicine at the University Hospital Bonn.

Additionally, written informed consent must be obtained from the parents or legal guardians prior to study inclusion.
Exclusion criteria:
1) Patients receiving palliative care.
2) Lack of written informed consent from the parents or legal guardians.
3) Contraindications to electrical impedance tomography (EIT) measurements according to the manufacturer's instructions for use (e.g., implanted cardiac pacemaker).
4) Inability to perform thoracic EIT measurements, for example, due to extensive wound dressings or indwelling thoracic drains.
